issue.title: FPE crash when progress bar enabled
issue.body:
### What happens?

When using the DuckLake and SQLite extensions, DuckDB crashes when the progress bar is enabled and runs OK when it is not

### To Reproduce

```
.timer on

PRAGMA disable_progress_bar; --enable this to cause crash
PRAGMA explain_output='all';

INSTALL ducklake;
LOAD ducklake;
INSTALL sqlite;
LOAD sqlite;

SET memory_limit='1GB';
SET threads=1;
SET temp_directory='./tempfiles';

ATTACH 'ducklake:sqlite:metadata.sqlite' AS dl (DATA_PATH 'data_files/');

CREATE TABLE dl.metars AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('../raw_metars') LIMIT 0;

ALTER TABLE dl.metars SET PARTITIONED BY (YEAR(timeObs), MONTH(timeObs));
ALTER TABLE dl.metars SET SORTED BY (stationName ASC, timeObs ASC);

CALL dl.set_option('parquet_compression', 'zstd');
CALL dl.set_option('parquet_compression_level', 12);

INSERT INTO dl.metars SELECT * FROM read_parquet('../raw_metars/') ;
```

When I `cat` this into duckdb, eg `cat create.sql | duckdb`


Produces this crash when I run it with gdb:

```Thread 1 "duckdb" received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.
0x0000000000894cc7 in duckdb_shell::ShellProgressBarDisplay::PrintProgressInternal(int, double, bool) ()
(gdb) bt
#0  0x0000000000894cc7 in duckdb_shell::ShellProgressBarDisplay::PrintProgressInternal(int, double, bool) ()
#1  0x000000000095e108 in duckdb::TerminalProgressBarDisplay::Update(double)
    ()
#2  0x000000000095a605 in duckdb::ProgressBar::Update(bool) ()
#3  0x0000000000d6e8c5 in duckdb::ClientContext::ExecuteTaskInternal(duckdb::ClientContextLock&, duckdb::BaseQueryResult&, bool) ()
#4  0x0000000000d6eaac in duckdb::PendingQueryResult::ExecuteInternal(duckdb::ClientContextLock&) ()
#5  0x0000000000d6ec56 in duckdb::PendingQueryResult::Execute() ()
#6  0x0000000000d72b10 in duckdb::ClientContext::Query(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>, duckdb::QueryParameters) ()
#7  0x0000000000d7356d in duckdb::Connection::SendQuery(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>, duckdb::QueryParameters) ()
#8  0x000000000085bd13 in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ExecuteStatement(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>) ()
#9  0x000000000085c017 in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ExecuteSQL(std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&) ()
#10 0x000000000085c31b in duckdb_shell::ShellState::RunOneSqlLine(duckdb_shell::InputMode, char*) ()
#11 0x0000000000866e8e in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ProcessInput(duckdb_shell::InputMode) ()
#12 0x000000000086827e in RunShell(int, char const**) ()
#13 0x00000000008388df in main ()```

### OS:

$ uname -a Linux  6.14.0-29-generic #29~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Aug 14 16:52:50 UTC 2 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### DuckDB Version:

v1.5.2 (Variegata) 8a5851971f

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Hardware:

_No response_

### Full Name:

John Jensen

### Affiliation:

None

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

No - I cannot easily share my data sets due to their large size

comments.body:
Thanks for opening this issue in the DuckDB issue tracker! To resolve this issue, our team needs a reproducible example. This includes:

* A source code snippet which reproduces the issue.
* The snippet should be self-contained, i.e., it should contain all imports and should use relative paths instead of hard coded paths (please avoid `/Users/JohnDoe/...`).
* A lot of issues can be reproduced with plain SQL code executed in the [DuckDB command line client](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/overview). If you can provide such an example, it greatly simplifies the reproduction process and likely results in a faster fix.
* If the script needs additional data, please share the data as a CSV, JSON, or Parquet file. Unfortunately, we cannot fix issues that can only be reproduced with a confidential data set. [Support contracts](https://duckdblabs.com/#support) allow sharing confidential data with the core DuckDB team under NDA.

For more detailed guidelines on how to create reproducible examples, please visit Stack Overflow's ["Minimal, Reproducible Example"](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) page.

I just tried your TPC-H example and it works, but my parquet example still core dumps with the same ProgressBar error. Odd. It's using a directory with a few thousand parquet files, which I've verified are all valid / not corrupt.

 I'll see if I can pare this down to something smaller.

Unfortunately, I haven’t been able to reproduce the crash. I tested both on a MacBook with an M1 chip and 16GB RAM, and on an Ubuntu 24.04.1 EC2 instance (`c6i.4xlarge`), but neither setup reproduced the issue.

I have been able to reproduce the same (or an adjacent) problem _without_ DuckLake or SQLite. ## Steps to Reproduce I haven't been able to condense this down to a minimal example, so I had to dump my entire dataset. 1. Download the contents from the [gh22716](https://gh22716.s3.fr-par.scw.cloud) S3 bucket (8 GB) 2. Execute `duckdb duck.db < load.sql` 3. Watch it burn ``` gh22716 ├── raw │ ├── chunk-01/ │ ├── chunk-02/ │ ├── chunk-03/ │ ├── chunk-04/ │ ├── mapping.tsv │ └── sequences.tsv └── load.sql ```
load.sql

```sql -- uncomment the following line to cause the script to NOT crash -- SET enable_progress_bar = false; create or replace macro load_port(__port_name, __parquet_file) as table select * exclude (_measurement, device_uid, iface, logger, port_name, port_id) from read_parquet('raw/chunk-*/pyric/' || __parquet_file) where "port_name" = __port_name order by _time; -------------------------------- create or replace table heartbeat as select * from load_port('heartbeat', 'uavcan.node.Heartbeat.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table dynamics as select _time, node_id, "value.force" as torque, "value.kinematics.acceleration" as acceleration, "value.kinematics.base.velocity" as velocity, "value.kinematics.base.position" as position, from load_port('dynamics', 'zubax.physics.dynamics.DoF3rdTs.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table power as select _time, node_id, "value.voltage" as voltage, "value.current" as current, from load_port('power', 'zubax.physics.electricity.PowerTs.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table feedback as select _time, node_id, demand_factor_pct, "heartbeat.health" as health, "heartbeat.readiness" as readiness, from load_port('feedback', 'zubax.service.actuator.Feedback.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table status as select _time, node_id, controller_temperature, error_count, "fault_flags.configuration", "fault_flags.overload", "fault_flags.other", from load_port('status', 'zubax.service.actuator.Status.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table compact as select * exclude (app_name) from load_port('compact', 'zubax.telega.CompactFeedback.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table dq as select _time, node_id, "voltage[0]" as vd, "voltage[1]" as vq, "current[0]" as id, "current[1]" as iq, from load_port('dq', 'zubax.telega.DQ.1.0.parquet'); create or replace table temperature as select * exclude (app_name) from load_port('temperature', 'zubax.telega.Temperatures.1.0.parquet'); -------------------------------- create or replace table setpoint as with setpoint_velocity as ( select * exclude (app_name, node_id) from load_port('setpoint_velocity', 'zubax.primitive.real16.Vector6.1.0.parquet') ) unpivot setpoint_velocity on "value[0]" as "1", "value[1]" as "3", "value[2]" as "5", "value[3]" as "7", "value[4]" as "9", "value[5]" as "11" into name node_id value velocity; -------------------------------- create or replace table supply as select _time, voltage, current, power from read_parquet('raw/chunk-*/sm15k/supply.parquet') order by _time; -------------------------------- create or replace table mapping as select "Rotation" as rotation, "Node ID" as node_id, "PX4 Signal" as px4_signal, from read_csv('raw/mapping.tsv') order by all; create or replace table sequences as select row_number() over (order by "Start") as id, "Rotation" as rotation, "Start"::timestamptz as start, "End"::timestamptz as end, from read_csv('raw/sequences.tsv') order by id; ```

The crash can be avoided by disabling the progress bar. ## Environment DuckDB CLI v1.5.2 (Variegata) 8a5851971f (Python venv duckdb_cli), x86_64, Fedora (kernel 7.x). The process exits with SIGFPE (signal 8); systemd-coredump writes a large core (~1.7 GiB). ## Stack (main thread, from coredumpctl) 1. duckdb_shell::ShellProgressBarDisplay::PrintProgressInternal 2. duckdb::TerminalProgressBarDisplay::Update 3. duckdb::ProgressBar::Update 4. duckdb::ClientContext::ExecuteTaskInternal → query execution

FWIW when I was working with Claude to try and figure out what was going on, it pointed this out:

``` The crash is entirely inside the progress bar rendering code, not the query engine:
ShellProgressBarDisplay::PrintProgressInternal(int, double, bool)
  └─ TerminalProgressBarDisplay::Update(double)
       └─ ProgressBar::Update(bool)
The division by zero is happening when the progress bar tries to calculate a percentage or bar width — 
almost certainly dividing by terminal width, total row count, or elapsed time, one of which is coming back as zero.

.
.
.

The strace log showed this earlier:
ioctl(0, TIOCGWINSZ, 0x7ffd126f5cd8) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)

ENOTTY means DuckDB couldn't query the terminal size because stdin is a pipe (cat file | duckdb), not a real terminal. The TIOCGWINSZ call failed, likely leaving the width as 0, and then PrintProgressInternal divided by it.

```

If that's the case, then the "environment" within which the CLI is running -- ie the terminal emulator -- may be the relevant differentiator between seeing the crash or not. FWIW mine have occurred in `gnome-terminal`, sometimes over an ssh session.

> The division by zero is happening when the progress bar tries to calculate a percentage or bar width

We had a similar issue before, but it was fixed in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/21591. We’ve just released version `1.5.3`. Could you please try using this version and let me know if the issue has been resolved?

Version 1.5.3 unfortunately does **not** fix the issue I observed. 

The issue seems to be directly caused by the stdin input, however:

```console
$ duckdb-v1.5.3 gh22716.db  < load.sql  # crashes
$ duckdb-v1.5.3 gh22716.db -f load.sql  # works
$ duckdb-v1.5.2 gh22716.db  < load.sql  # crashes
$ duckdb-v1.5.2 gh22716.db -f load.sql  # works
$ duckdb-v1.5.1 gh22716.db  < load.sql  # crashes
$ duckdb-v1.5.1 gh22716.db -f load.sql  # works
```

I haven't tested against v1.5.0 because it had an issue with inputs from non-interactive shells, which was [fixed in v1.5.1](https://duckdb.org/2026/03/23/announcing-duckdb-151#non-interactive-shell).

## Reproducible Example

I've managed to boil this down to a minimal, locally reproducible example:

### Setup

Create a sample parquet dataset and a minimal query file:

```sql
D copy (select "range" as r from range(1_000_000_000)) to 'range.parquet';
```

```sql
-- query.sql
select r % 10, count(*) from 'range.parquet' group by all;
```

### Reproduce

As observed above, piping from stdin fails, while executing via `-f` works:

```console
$ duckdb --version                                                          
v1.5.3 (Variegata) 14eca11bd9

$ duckdb -f query.sql 
┌──────────┬──────────────┐
│ (r % 10) │ count_star() │
│  int64   │    int64     │
├──────────┼──────────────┤
│        0 │    100000000 │
│        2 │    100000000 │
│        5 │    100000000 │
│        9 │    100000000 │
│        1 │    100000000 │
│        3 │    100000000 │
│        4 │    100000000 │
│        6 │    100000000 │
│        7 │    100000000 │
│        8 │    100000000 │
└──────────┴──────────────┘
  10 rows       2 columns

$ duckdb < query.sql
[1]    5092 floating point exception (core dumped)  duckdb < query.sql
```

I’m unable to reproduce this issue on either macOS or Ubuntu (on an EC2 instance), so there may be some differences in our environments. Could you share more details about the environment where you’re seeing this issue? Any relevant configuration info would be helpful.

I've been able to reproduce the issue on a Scaleway [PLAY2-NANO](https://www.scaleway.com/en/pricing/virtual-instances-pricing/) instance (2 vCPUs, 4 GB RAM), running Fedora 43, accessed via SSH from Fedora 44 using the standard terminal emulator.

On my laptop (Lenovo ThinkPad E14 Gen 7, Intel Core Ultra 7 255H, 32 GiB RAM) running Fedora 44, the example above works, but I can reproduce the issue by increasing the scale to `range(10_000_000_000)`.

@Finwood yes, your example crashes for me on my slower (i5 CPU) machine, but works OK on my ~5x faster (Ryzen 7) machine. That implies to me that it has something to do with time/duration.

I built 1.5.3 from source, got the error, and printed a stack trace:

```
#0  0x000057f46a221c3f in duckdb_shell::ShellProgressBarDisplay::PrintProgressInternal(int, double, bool) ()
#1  0x000057f46a3089ac in duckdb::TerminalProgressBarDisplay::Update(double) ()
#2  0x000057f46a3046fd in duckdb::ProgressBar::Update(bool) ()
#3  0x000057f46a731afc in duckdb::ClientContext::ExecuteTaskInternal(duckdb::ClientContextLock&, duckdb::BaseQueryResult&, bool) ()
#4  0x000057f46a731d84 in duckdb::PendingQueryResult::ExecuteInternal(duckdb::ClientContextLock&) ()
#5  0x000057f46a731f9a in duckdb::PendingQueryResult::Execute() ()
#6  0x000057f46a734ac8 in duckdb::ClientContext::Query(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>, duckdb::QueryParameters) ()
#7  0x000057f46a735574 in duckdb::Connection::SendQuery(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>, duckdb::QueryParameters)
    ()
#8  0x000057f46a1e883b in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ExecuteStatement(duckdb::unique_ptr<duckdb::SQLStatement, std::default_delete<duckdb::SQLStatement>, true>) ()
#9  0x000057f46a1ec08d in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ExecuteSQL(std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&) ()
#10 0x000057f46a1ec3bb in duckdb_shell::ShellState::RunOneSqlLine(duckdb_shell::InputMode, char*) ()
#11 0x000057f46a1f5146 in duckdb_shell::ShellState::ProcessInput(duckdb_shell::InputMode) ()
#12 0x000057f46a1f631a in RunShell(int, char const**) ()
#13 0x000057f46a1d6459 in main ()
```
I managed to reproduce the issue and put up a PR to fix it. Thanks both for pointing it out!

issue.title: fix progress bar output and crash when piping SQL

repository.name: duckdb
repository.description: DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system

issue.body:
When running `duckdb < query.sql`, the progress bar produced a lot of trailing spaces per update line and on some occasions crashed with a floating point exception. When stdin is a pipe or file, `ioctl` fails and leaves the width uninitialized, returning a garbage value (or zero). The progress bar then attempted to render a line of that width, causing an arithmetic overflow and SIGFPE.

Using a default value of 120 feels a bit hacky, but we already follow the same approach in `BoxRendererImplementation::Initialize()`, so I applied it here as well for consistency.

Fixes: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/22716

timeline.body: I managed to reproduce the issue and put up a PR to fix it. Thanks both for pointing it out!
